transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-07-21
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 mins (recording)
- Attendees: Maya Collins (Redwood AE), Rajat Singh (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (BlueCove Head of Risk), Daniel Ortiz (Platform Eng), Hannah Li (Security Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- BlueCove evaluating whether Redwood Hosted or Dedicated/Private fits regulatory needs for EU customers and certain US healthcare customers. Main asks: strict residency, minimal logs, BAA/HIPAA posture, KMS/HSM integration, ability to disable telemetry, audit logs retention controls.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, I'll kick us off. Welcome BlueCove team.
[00:00:08] Priya: Hi Maya, thanks. We'll be tight on time but wanted to get through compliance fit questions.
[00:00:15] Daniel: Yep hi, Daniel here. We'll focus on residency and what gets logged.
[00:00:22] Rajat: Quick intro — Rajat on infra at Redwood, I'll cover network and private deploy details.
[00:00:30] Hannah: Hey all. Security lead, mostly questions on KMS and auditability.

[00:01:05] Maya: Big picture — BlueCove has EU customers and a small set of US healthcare partners where HIPAA could apply. You're evaluating Hosted first but want Dedicated/Private options if residency or logs are blockers, is that right?
[00:01:18] Priya: That's right. For EU accounts we need all customer data to stay in EU zones — processing and persistent storage. For the healthcare integrator we need BAA and assurances about PHI handling.
[00:01:32] Maya: Got it. Quick Q — do you already have a cloud provider preference for private deployments?
[00:01:38] Daniel: We're primarily on GCP in EU-west1; we prefer VPC peering and customer-managed keys.

[00:02:10] Rajat: On the Hosted side, our EU region is run on dedicated tenancy in eu-west1, but Hosted telemetry and some audit events may be retained in our control plane. We can provide truncation/redaction options and exportable audit logs.
[00:02:26] Hannah: When you say telemetry — can you enumerate? We need to know whether prompts, outputs, embeddings, or full payloads are stored and for how long.
[00:02:38] Rajat: Sure — rough breakdown: request metadata (timestamps, model, route) and observability metrics are collected for 90 days by default. Payloads — prompts and generated tokens — are not stored long-term in Hosted unless retention is enabled for debugging; retention windows are configurable and can be disabled for EU customers with contractual terms. 
[00:03:05] Priya: "Can be disabled" is a bit vague — we need contractual guarantees that PII/PHI won't be retained in Redwood logs for EU/PHI customers unless explicitly turned on by us. Also need ability to run on Dedicated or Private where everything stays in our VPC.
[00:03:20] Maya: Absolutely. For customers with strict residency or HIPAA we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Dedicated gives you predictable capacity in our hardware pools but logs still pass through Redwood control plane. Private puts control plane in your VPC or on-prem — full data plane separation.
[00:03:40] Daniel: So with Private, all prompts and responses stay inside our network? No egress to Redwood-managed services?
[00:03:46] Rajat: Correct — Redwood Private can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane. There are air-gapped on-prem options too. In that model audit logs, metrics and prompts need to be routed to your chosen sinks — we can disable telemetry to Redwood.
[00:04:05] Hannah: KMS — do you integrate with Cloud KMS / HSM and can we bring keys? We require envelope encryption with customer keys.
[00:04:13] Rajat: Yes, we support customer-managed keys. For GCP we integrate with Cloud KMS; similarly we support AWS KMS and on-prem HSMs with PKCS11. There's a note in the docs about key rotation and access controls.
[00:04:30] Priya: For HIPAA we need a BAA and to ensure logs with PHI aren't retained; PRAs for log redaction. Can Redwood sign a BAA?
[00:04:38] Maya: We do execute BAAs; we have customers in healthcare. I'll share our HIPAA pack and the legal contacts. We'll need to scope the PII types to confirm exceptions.

[00:05:15] Daniel: A couple of architecture-y questions — does KV cache or any model cache leave the customer boundary? We saw notes about KV caching to improve latency.
[00:05:23] Rajat: Default caching is ephemeral in the serving layer. For Hosted it can be shared across instances to increase efficiency, but we can disable cross-tenant caching for regulated customers. For Private, caches remain inside your deployment.
[00:05:40] Priya: What about embeddings? We generate embeddings for search — those might contain customer data. Can embeddings be hashed or stored only locally?
[00:05:49] Rajat: Embeddings are treated like model outputs; by default Hosted may persist them for a short period for indexing features, but again for regulated customers we can disable that or recommend Dedicated/Private. We can also support redaction or one-way hashing on ingestion if you want an extra layer.

[00:06:30] Hannah: Audit trail — we need immutable logs for access and config changes for at least 2 years. Do you provide that, and in which format?
[00:06:38] Maya: We surface audit logs as exportable JSON events to sinks like BigQuery, S3, or a SIEM. Retention is configurable; for Dedicated/Private we can implement customer retention policies.
[00:06:52] Daniel: How about realtime tracing for debugging — will traces include PII?
[00:06:58] Rajat: Traces include request IDs and timing info; payload inclusion is optional. We can scrub or mask payloads before exporting traces.

[00:07:40] Priya: Data residency nuances — if a EU user hits the service, is any part of processing routed through US control-plane? We cannot have any control-plane data cross borders.
[00:07:50] Rajat: For Hosted, some control plane metadata may be centralized; but we have EU-only deployments and can contractually commit to EU-only control plane and storage. For strict customers, Private is the safest; Dedicated can be region-bound but control plane is still Redwood-managed unless we do a VPC-hosted control plane.
[00:08:10] Maya: Important to note: we can provide EU-residency guarantees in contract and can disable retention of payloads in the control plane.

[00:09:00] Hannah: Pen testing and compliance artifacts — we need SOC2 type II report and past pen test results. Also do you do regular vulnerability scans?
[00:09:07] Maya: Yes — we'll share SOC2 Type II, ISO where available, and a summary of third-party pen test results. We run scheduled scans and agent-based security checks; I'll include the schedule and contact for the security team.

[00:09:50] Daniel: Network connectivity for Private — can we do a peered VPC with no public ingress? We want egress controls and private endpoints.
[00:09:58] Rajat: Yes — Private supports VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints, and firewall/NACL controls. You can lock down to internal ranges.

[00:10:30] Priya: A risk question — if we choose Dedicated, and Redwood manages the control plane, are there administrative logs that could contain full prompt text? We need assurance those are not accessible.
[00:10:40] Rajat: In Dedicated, by default the control plane retains minimal metadata. Prompt text retention is opt-in for debugging. For higher assurance we recommend Private or contractual controls with encryption at rest + limited access.

[00:11:25] Maya: Quick aside — cost tradeoffs. Hosted is simplest and lower upfront; Dedicated requires reservation but gives more isolation; Private is largest lift but best for compliance.
[00:11:35] Daniel: Pricing aside, timeline — if we wanted a pilot, what does typical onboarding look like?
[00:11:41] Maya: For Hosted pilot you can be up in days. Dedicated pilot — we size GPUs, test throughput, ~2–4 weeks to provision. Private on-premish depends — often 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and HSM provisioning.

[00:12:20] Priya: On eDiscovery — regulators may request logs. If we disable payload retention, how do we support investigations?
[00:12:28] Rajat: We propose a compromise: keep metadata and redacted payloads by default. For investigations we can enable extended retention with strict access controls and audit trails. All of that would be contractual for regulated customers.

[00:13:10] Hannah: Are there examples of customers in banking or fintech with similar constraints?
[00:13:15] Maya: Yes — we have multiple finance customers using Dedicated and Private with EU residency and export controls. I'll anonymize and share case studies.

[00:13:45] Priya: Encryption at rest/in transit — TLS for transit is standard, and for at-rest we need AES-256 with customer keys. Also we'd like HSM-backed signatures for audit logs.
[00:13:56] Rajat: AES-256 is used; HSM-backed key management is supported in Private and Dedicated via BYOK patterns. Audit log signing is possible if you want append-only signed logs.

[00:14:40] Daniel: Is there any PII that might end up in monitoring dashboards (e.g., user IDs in error traces)?
[00:14:48] Rajat: Dashboards show aggregated metrics by default. We can mask IDs and avoid user-level PII on dashboards; raw traces can be redacted.

[00:15:20] Maya: Let's go scenario-based. Priya, can you describe a critical EU workflow that concerns you?
[00:15:28] Priya: Sure — onboarding flow where customers supply identity docs (SSNs, docs). The flow uses an internal review assistant that calls the model to summarize docs. We worry those docs might be logged or cached.
[00:15:42] Rajat: In that case we suggest Private or Dedicated with payload retention disabled; also implement client-side redaction or tokenization before sending to the model. We can provide hooks for tokenization libraries.
[00:16:05] Hannah: For HIPAA — if PHI is in prompts, we need to ensure Business Associate Agreement and also the ability to locate and delete PHI.
[00:16:14] Maya: Correct. We support subject data deletion and can provide APIs for data erasure. BAAs cover the obligations.

[00:16:50] Daniel: Ops question — how is model versioning handled? If there's a model regression that exposes PII via hallucination, what rollback and monitoring do we have?
[00:16:59] Rajat: Our rolling deploys support canary and A/B rollouts; you can pin model versions per route. We also provide quality monitoring and alerts for regressions tied to prompt sets.

[00:17:45] Priya: Licensing/legal question — data processor vs controller — we need Redwood to be the processor and we remain controller. Is that your standard position?
[00:17:53] Maya: Yes, for most customers Redwood acts as a processor and the customer is the controller. We document that in the DPA.

[00:18:25] Hannah: A small red team question — can we run a vulnerability assessment against a Dedicated instance?
[00:18:31] Rajat: For Dedicated we permit approved pen tests under a coordinated testing agreement. For Private on-prem you can do internal testing as you control the environment.

[00:19:05] Daniel: For Private, what are the minimum hw specs? We run inference on A100-ish clusters — is Redwood runtime compatible?
[00:19:13] Rajat: Our runtime supports Nvidia A100, H100 and some ARM-based devices. We'll send a compatibility matrix. For Private we have validated builds for A100 clusters.

[00:19:45] Priya: Back to logs retention length — you said default 90 days — can we set 30 days or even 0?
[00:19:53] Rajat: Yes — for Hosted we can lower retention to 30 days via config; to achieve 0 you'd need a Private deployment or contractual terms to disable retention.

[00:20:30] Maya: Sounds like action items — we'll share SOC2 + HIPAA docs and recommended architecture. Rajat will prepare Private topology. BlueCove to share regulated field list.

[00:21:00] Priya: Quick note — in our procurement we will want indemnities around data leakage — will need legal to review BAA and terms.
[00:21:07] Maya: Understood. We'll route legal to legal.

[00:21:40] (longer technical back-and-forth omitted)

[00:35:00] Rajat: (demoing a slide) Here's a sample Private network diagram — you see the control plane sits in your VPC and the serving fleet is subnet-bound. Telemetry is toggled at the ingress.
[00:40:12] Daniel: If we use on-prem, what's the upgrade story? Microservice updates and security patches?
[00:40:20] Rajat: We provide an upgrade runbook; for on-prem there's an operator that pulls signed images from Redwood-approved registries. We coordinate maintenance windows.

[00:48:00] Priya: One final question — residency certification. Do you have third-party certification or attestation for EU-only operations?
[00:48:09] Maya: We can provide attestations and region-specific controls; for strict regulatory audits we'd produce a tailored report.

[00:55:30] Hannah: And SLAs for Dedicated/Private?
[00:55:36] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA commitments for uptime and latency tiers; Private SLAs vary based on deployment model and support level.

[01:00:00] Maya: OK let's recap next steps — we'll share security artifacts, Rajat will do the deep dive and diagram, BlueCove will send PII lists, and we'll scope pilot pricing.
[01:00:12] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[01:00:18] Daniel: Thanks.
[01:00:22] Hannah: Thanks.

[01:01:00] Maya: We'll follow up via email with the pack and proposed times for the technical call.

(End of transcript: recording ends ~62 minutes)
